notes.text: Jonathan Marchessault is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-six forward.

Nicolas Hague has not dressed for the last 4 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Daemon Hunt has taken his spot beside Jayden Struble. That pair has had 44% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 47:17 together, up from 29% with Hague.
Shane Wright joined from SEA on Nov 2 and has played beside Filip Forsberg and Nils Höglander.
Adam Edström has started killing penalties: on the ice for 33% of the team’s shorthanded time in 17 games, up from 1% with his old team last season.
Kevin Fiala is out week to week and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Mats Zuccarello is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 6 games.
Erik Gustafsson is day to day, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-pair defenseman.
Alex Turcotte returned in their last game after missing 11 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Kenny Connors was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Erik Haula and Joel Armia.

stakes: The Predators go in tied for fourth in the Central with 21 points, the Kings seventh in the Pacific with 12 points.

LAK.head: The Kings have a lot going for them
LAK.body: Even though Los Angeles will be without Fiala, the Kings have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Predators’ way back in is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: Haula meets his old team
paras: The Kings (5-8-2) lost 5-2 to Pittsburgh on Saturday, while the Predators have won four straight. Going in, the Predators are fourth in the Central (tied for 12th in the NHL) and the Kings seventh in the Pacific (30th).

The Predators’ record (.618) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.535), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. The Kings have played better than their record (.400) says: their chances are worth about .622, mostly because they’re 2-5 in one-goal games.

The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest), get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st) and give up a lot of shots (31st). As for the Kings, they leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest), keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st) and lean hard on their top players (4th lowest). The Kings hound the puck, but the Preds sit back.

Filip Forsberg (5 G / 15 A / 20 P in 17 GP) leads the Predators in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Steven Stamkos (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 17 GP) has a team-high ten goals. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Adrian Kempe (6 G / 7 A / 13 P in 14 GP) isn’t far behind.

Nashville has two options in net: Juuse Saros (5-3-4 / .912 SV% in 12 GS) and Justus Annunen (3-1-0 / .873 SV% in 4 GS). Saros has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Saturday. Los Angeles also has two options: Darcy Kuemper (5-4-1 / .878 SV% in 10 GS) and Anton Forsberg (0-4-1 / .902 SV% in 5 GS). Kuemper has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Saturday. For both teams, it’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Peter Laviolette likes to send Moore, Byfield and Perry out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Stamkos, O'Reilly and Bourque.
